statements.text: Carmen, our Google Ads lead, was going through a venue client's search terms with a member of their team recently, and another venue's name came up.
statements.source: Carmen, our Google Ads lead, was looking through the searches with someone from the venue's team.
statements.why: Matches the brief.

statements.text: Carmen's usual starting point with competitor searches is to leave them in.
statements.why: Carmen said her default is to leave competitors in.

statements.text: The team member agreed that made sense for this one, because couples had told them they were looking at that venue too.
statements.source: And when a nearby venue came up, that team member explained that some couples had considered that place before considering theirs.
statements.why: The sources say couples had considered the venue. They do not say couples told the team, and they do not say couples were still looking at it.

statements.text: Carmen's reply was simple: "Okay, good to know."
statements.why: The quote is word for word, but the evidence places it after the other-market exchange (the Hamptons venue). It was not a reply to the nearby-venue comparison.

statements.text: A little later in the review, a different venue came up. This time the team member explained that it served a different market.
statements.source: Later in the discussion, they identified another venue as serving a different market, without the same overlap.
statements.why: Matches the brief.

statements.text: "That's nowhere near," she said.
statements.why: Erin said it. The quote is accurate.

statements.text: Couples choosing that venue weren't weighing it against theirs, and Carmen agreed that one should be excluded.
statements.why: Agreement is kept as a recommendation, not a completed change.

statements.text: So there were two venue names in the same report and two different recommendations. What separated them came from the venue's team, not from the account.
statements.source: The useful distinction came from combining the searches with what the client's team knew.
statements.why: Matches the brief.

statements.text: We bring the advertising expertise and take responsibility for the recommendation.
statements.source: Carmen brought her advertising judgment; the client's team brought information...
statements.why: The brief gives Carmen's judgment, not a commitment to take responsibility for recommendations. This is not in the belief statements.

statements.text: Our Google Search Accelerator ... we build and launch your campaigns, and you run them with our experts beside you.
statements.why: Matches the approved descriptor. It makes no claim that this client joined.

statements.text: Our Google Ads lead, Carmen, was going through a venue client's search terms with someone from their team, and another venue's name popped up.
statements.source: Carmen, our Google Ads lead, was looking through the searches with someone from the venue's team.
statements.why: Matches the brief.

statements.text: In her words, "my default is always just leave competitors in."
statements.why: Matches the quote except for a dropped filler word.

statements.text: And the team member said, yeah, that makes sense here, because couples had told them they'd considered that venue too.
statements.source: And when a nearby venue came up, that team member explained that some couples had considered that place before considering theirs.
statements.why: Adds that couples told the team. The words attributed to the team member are also invented dialogue.

statements.text: A different venue came up. She said, "That's nowhere near." Different market. Those couples weren't comparing the two venues. So Carmen agreed that one should be excluded.
statements.why: Matches the evidence and the brief.

statements.text: The thing that made the difference wasn't anywhere in the account. It was what the venue's team hears from couples.
statements.source: The useful distinction came from combining the searches with what the client's team knew.
statements.why: Matches the brief.

statements.text: Caption: One nearby venue made sense to leave in, because couples had mentioned considering it alongside theirs.
statements.source: The client's team knew couples had considered one nearby venue as well as theirs.
statements.why: Adds that couples mentioned it to the team, and says the venue was left in. The sources give Carmen's default but no decision to keep it.

statements.text: Caption: Another, the team explained, was in a different market entirely. Carmen agreed that one should be excluded.
statements.why: Matches the brief.

statements.text: We saw this in a recent review. One nearby venue, the client's team knew couples had considered alongside theirs. Another, they told Carmen, was a different market entirely, and she agreed that one should be excluded.
statements.source: The client's team knew couples had considered one nearby venue as well as theirs. They placed another in a different market.
statements.why: Matches the brief.

statements.text: We take responsibility for the advertising recommendation.
statements.why: The sources give no such commitment.

statements.text: Caption: In a review with one of our venue clients, the team explained that couples had considered one nearby venue as well as theirs. A second venue served a different market, and Carmen agreed with excluding it.
statements.why: Matches the brief.

statements.text: Caption: We bring the expertise and stand behind the recommendation.
statements.why: Adds an accountability claim the sources do not give.

statements.text: Two other venues showed up in a client's Google Ads search terms.
statements.source: Other venue names appeared in the discussion.
statements.why: Matches the brief.

statements.text: The venue's team knew couples had also considered one of them.
statements.source: The client's team knew couples had considered one nearby venue as well as theirs.
statements.why: Matches the brief.

statements.text: The other served a different market, so our Google Ads lead agreed that one should be excluded.
statements.source: Carmen agreed it should be excluded.
statements.why: Matches the brief.

statements.text: Caption: The team knew couples had looked at one nearby venue too, so that search had a real reason to be there... the team explained it was nowhere near their market. Carmen agreed it should be excluded.
statements.source: So there was a reason to give that search some consideration.
statements.why: Matches the brief and the evidence.

statements.text: Carmen, our Google Ads lead, was going through a venue client's search terms with a member of their team. Other venues' names were on the list. Her default with competitor searches is to keep them running.
statements.why: Matches the brief and the evidence.

statements.text: The team member said keeping it made sense. Couples had told them they'd considered that venue as well as theirs.
statements.source: The client's team knew couples had considered one nearby venue as well as theirs.
statements.why: Adds that couples told the team. The sources do not say the team said keeping it made sense, or that the venue was kept.

statements.text: Carmen's reply: "Okay, good to know."
statements.why: The quote was said after the other-market exchange, not after the nearby-venue comparison.

statements.text: Then another venue came up. The team member explained it served a different market. Its couples weren't weighing the two. Carmen agreed that one should be excluded.
statements.why: Matches the brief.

statements.text: We take responsibility for the advertising recommendation.
statements.why: The sources give no such commitment.

statements.text: The Google Search Accelerator ... We launch your campaigns, then guide you while you run them.
statements.why: Matches the approved descriptor.

statements.text: Some owners want us to manage their ads. Others want us to launch their campaigns and guide them as they take over.
statements.why: Describes both offers consistently with the descriptors.

statements.text: Caption: Carmen heard two different explanations from a member of a venue client's team. Couples had considered one nearby venue alongside theirs. A second served a market the team didn't see overlapping with their own, and Carmen agreed with excluding it.
statements.source: During a search review, Carmen heard two different explanations from a member of the client's team.
statements.why: Matches the brief.

statements.text: Caption: ...with us standing behind the recommendation.
statements.why: Adds a responsibility claim the sources do not give.

statements.text: Carmen: "my default is always just leave competitors in."
statements.why: Verbatim apart from a dropped filler word.

statements.text: Carmen: "Okay, good to know." (email, carousel slide 3)
statements.why: The words are accurate, but the pack uses them as a reply to the nearby-venue comparison. The evidence places them elsewhere.

statements.text: Erin: "That's nowhere near."
statements.why: Verbatim, with the correct speaker.
